headline: UKMTO reports tanker struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz with onboard fire; IRGC separately claims mine strike
source_time_text: FF Latest Stories '10 min ago' at observed 2026-10-10 ~23:40 UTC; derived FF publication ~23:29 UTC ±15m. Anadolu relays UKMTO master's 10 Oct 22:20 TRT (19:20 UTC) incident report. Separate IRGC mine claim earlier on Oct 10 may describe same hull but matching not independently established.

evidence.dominant_driver: A UKMTO-reported tanker was hit on its port side by an unknown projectile and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. This independently supports a maritime incident but not IRGC attribution or its mine narrative; exact hull identity and link to IRGC claim remain uncertain.

market_expectations.distribution_notes: Geopolitical maritime attacks already common and partially reflected in Friday energy risk premium; specific Saturday event cannot be measured while markets are closed.

absorption.reason: General Hormuz risk partly priced before weekend; new incident-specific reaction cannot be observed until markets reopen. No inference of price action from Friday settlement.

observations.local_markets: Weekend closed; no post-event 15m/1h/4h completed bars

evidence.decision_notes: UKMTO ship master's report 10 Oct 19:20 UTC relayed by Anadolu on Oct 11; Forex Factory first discovered ~23:30 UTC Oct 10. UKMTO primary product not directly accessible. IRGC claim mine, UKMTO reports unknown projectile: do not conflate attribution. Backfilled and excluded from hit-rate because incident age >4h and all target markets closed. Fixed intraday horizons not rolled to Monday. No hindsight. M2 next_session forecasts conditional and low confidence.
